target.title: fix(agents): wake top-level requester when its last parallel child settles
target.body:
Closes #99395

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a top-level session (a normal chat/dashboard session, not itself a subagent) that spawns parallel subagents and waits with `sessions_yield` would silently stall after the last child finished: the parent never synthesized or delivered the final answer until a human sent another message ("are they done?"). Any fan-out-then-aggregate workflow is affected — e.g. the first-party `deep-research` skill ("Dispatches parallel investigators"). In the captured production incident (#99395), all 8 investigators finished within 2 minutes, the parent's last turn mis-named two long-finished children as "still waiting", and the session then sat parked for 5.5 minutes of total silence until a user ping rescued it. Results whose completion announce gave up (`NO_REPLY` retry exhaustion) were never heard at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime's "all descendants settled → continue and send your final answer" wake (`wakeSubagentRunAfterDescendants`, from the nested-orchestrator fix #97090) only targets orchestrators that have a subagent-registry run record; a top-level session has none, and the passive per-child announces give it no reliable way to know the batch drained (the injected `## Active Subagents` block vanishes at zero-active, and completion events carry no outstanding count). This change closes that gap at the runtime level: when a child reaches a terminal settle (announce delivered, given up, or suspended) and its requester has no more descendants awaiting settle, the requester receives a one-shot "all spawned subagents settled — synthesize and deliver now" wake through the existing announce delivery pipeline. Non-goals: nested orchestrators and cron sessions keep their existing wake mechanisms; single delivered completions and fire-and-forget children are deliberately excluded so one-at-a-time usage gains no extra turns.

## User Impact

Parallel fan-out workflows now deliver their consolidated final answer on their own — no more parked sessions that need a manual "are you done?" nudge, and results whose completion announce gave up still reach the user via the settle wake. Sequential single-subagent usage, fire-and-forget spawns, nested orchestrators, and cron jobs behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Focused unit tests** (new `src/agents/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.test.ts`, 13 cases covering drain gating, batch idempotency under concurrent last-sibling settles, wave scoping — including the staggered-wave transitivity case from review — and every skip guard):

```
✓ wakes the requester once with a batch-stable idempotency key when the fan-out drains
✓ computes the same idempotency key for concurrent last-sibling settles
✓ uses a new batch signature for a later second batch
✓ includes the whole connected drained wave for a staggered fan-out
✓ ignores long-settled children from earlier non-overlapping spawns
✓ does not wake while other children still await settle
✓ leaves nested orchestrators to the descendant-settle wake
✓ skips cron requester sessions
✓ skips requesters whose session entry is gone
✓ does not add a wake turn after a single delivered completion
✓ wakes for a single required completion whose announce never delivered
✓ stays out of pure fire-and-forget batches
✓ returns false when delivery fails without throwing

Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  13 passed (13)
```

**Full subagent unit + e2e sweep** (all 33 `src/agents/subagent-*` / `openclaw-tools.subagents.*` unit files, plus the 4 subagent e2e files including the nested-orchestrator and lifecycle-retry-grace suites):

```
Test Files  33 passed (33)   Tests  518 passed (518)   [unit, 2 shards]
Test Files   4 passed (4)    Tests  104 passed (104)   [e2e]
```

`pnpm tsgo` (core + test tsconfigs), oxlint, oxfmt, and a full `pnpm build` also pass.

**Give-up path proven in-repo:** `subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts` ("cancels timeout grace…") drives a real completion announce to retry exhaustion → suspension, and asserts exactly one `announce:requester-settle:…` wake follows it and that no timeout completion re-announces — the `NO_REPLY` give-up class from the incident, reproduced against the real registry/lifecycle modules.

**After-fix real-run proof #2 — the production failure class, rescued (2026-07-03, redacted):** a real gateway built from this branch, isolated state dir, real model (`claude-sonnet-4-6` via an OpenAI-compatible proxy), driven by exactly one user message: a deep-research skill task that fanned out **8 investigators in two batches** (5-concurrency staggering, one spawn attempt failed and was retried by the parent), each writing a multi-section report over ~5 minutes. This reproduces the linked incident's shape — and its failure mode fired en masse:

```
14:34:41  user sends the research task                        [the ONLY user message]
14:35:0x  parent spawns 8 investigators (2 batches), yields
14:40–14:53  11 child runs end (incl. parent-driven re-dispatches); EIGHT completion
          announces exhaust retries and give up ("completion agent did not produce a
          visible reply") — the parent NO_REPLYs essentially every completion event.
          On unpatched openclaw this session is now permanently parked.
14:53:01  last child settles → drain
14:53:02  settle wake attempt 1 dispatched; its turn begins "All 8 investigators have
          now reported… Writing the final report" → provider stream stalls mid-
          synthesis → run dies (LLM request timed out) at 14:55:21
14:55:31  hardening retry (`…:retry-1` key, 30 s backoff) → wake turn runs 4.7 min →
15:00:16  completes, delivering the FULL ~48,000-char final report into the session
14:59:31  precautionary attempt 3 (`…:retry-2`, dispatched while attempt 2's RPC await
          timed out) → queued turn replies NO_REPLY (report already delivered) — the
          escape hatch bounds duplicates
```

Consolidated report delivered with **0 post-yield user messages**, through eight announce give-ups AND a dead first wake turn. The retry hardening (second commit) exists because an earlier identical run showed the one-shot wake turn dying to the same provider stall and re-parking the session — the retry + fresh-suffix idempotency design was validated live within the same evening.

**After-fix real-run proof #1 — clean mechanics (2026-07-03, redacted):** same setup, one user message: *"Spawn exactly THREE subagents in parallel via sessions_spawn … sessions_yield … send one consolidated summary titled ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP."* No further input was sent. Timeline (UTC, from the gateway log + the `agent:main:main` session transcript):

```
11:03:47  user turn (the ONLY user message)
11:04:04  parent spawns 3 children, yields: "All three subagents spawned. Waiting for all to complete."
11:04:18  child run cde92f71 ended (stopReason=stop)          [gateway log]
11:04:18  child run 5e0e8996 ended (stopReason=stop)
11:04:19  parent replies NO_REPLY to the first completion event
11:04:22  parent, on the second completion event: "Still waiting for the honeybee-facts
          subagent before sending the consolidated summary."   [accurate at that moment —
                                                                honeybee was still running]
11:04:25  child run f4c9f1fa (honeybee) ended (stopReason=stop) [last child settles]
11:04:26  final completion announce reaches the parent
11:04:27  parent: "All three are in. Here's the consolidated summary: # ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP …"
11:04:45  run announce:requester-settle:agent:main:main:5e0e8996…,cde92f71…,f4c9f1fa… ended
          [the new settle wake — batch-stable idempotency key covering all 3 children, carrying
           "[Subagent Context] Every subagent spawned from this session has now settled … send your
           consolidated final answer to the user now" + all three children's findings]
11:04:45  parent replies NO_REPLY to the wake                   [answer already delivered — the
                                                                escape hatch suppressing a duplicate]
```

Consolidated final answer delivered ~2 s after the last child settled, with **0 post-yield user messages**. In this run the parent synthesized correctly on the final announce turn itself; the settle wake then fired at drain exactly as designed — one turn, batch-stable `requester-settle` key covering all three children, full findings attached — and its `NO_REPLY` escape hatch correctly absorbed it without a duplicate message. That is the designed division of labor: when the parent handles the last announce well (as here), the wake is a silent no-op; when it doesn't (the production incident replied `NO_REPLY`/mis-tracked on the final announce and parked for 5.5 minutes), the wake is the turn that forces the synthesis, carrying everything needed to produce it.

**Live observation (production, openclaw 2026.6.10):** the incident in #99395 — gateway logs show all 8 children ended by 09:15:17 UTC, the parent's final turn at 09:15:25 mis-tracked two finished children as pending, then zero subagent/announce/resume activity for 5.5 minutes until the user's 09:20:45 ping. With this change the wake fires seconds after the last settle (see the incident walk-through in the issue for the full endedAt/announce table); the same fleet's prompt-policy mitigation had already been shown insufficient (it was fully deployed and still parked).

**Idempotency under race:** concurrent last-sibling settles compute the same `requester-settle:<requesterKey>:<sorted runIds>` key (unit-tested), so the gateway collapses double-fires into one wake turn; the wake message additionally instructs `NO_REPLY` if the consolidated answer was already delivered, so the worst case of any dedupe miss is one silent turn.

**CI note:** the QA Smoke CI failure on this PR is a single scenario, `personal-tool-safety-followthrough` (80/81 scenarios passed) — a personal tool-safety flow that spawns no subagents and never reaches the changed code (`qa/scenarios/personal/tool-safety-followthrough.yaml` contains no `sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield`/subagent usage; the settle-wake trigger only fires from subagent-run finalize paths). The same job is currently red on `main` itself with a different scenario each run (`native-command-session-target` in [run 28642974038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28642974038) and [run 28641562098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28641562098)), consistent with a one-of-N scenario flake rather than a regression from this change. Happy to have the job re-run.

## Implementation notes

- **`hasDescendantRunAwaitingSettle`** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-queries.ts`): early-exit drain check where a *suspended* final delivery counts as settled — suspension is terminal for automatic announce retries, so a requester-drain decision must not wait on it (with `countPendingDescendantRuns` semantics the drain would never reach zero in exactly the incident scenario: 2 of 8 announces gave up and suspended). Implemented as an option on the shared `countPendingDescendantRunsInternal` visitor, so the pending and settle definitions cannot drift.
- **`maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled`** (`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`): scopes the wake batch to the settling child's **parallel wave — the connected component of lifetime overlaps** seeded at the settling run. Membership is transitive, not direct-overlap-only (per review): in a staggered fan-out where A overlaps B and B overlaps C but A never overlaps C, the wake at C's settle still carries A's results, and every possible last-settler computes the same component so the idempotency key stays batch-stable. Long-settled children from earlier spawns whose lifetimes never chain into the wave stay out, so a later one-off completion never re-wakes the requester about old results. Fires only for ≥ 2 required completions in the wave or ≥ 1 undelivered required completion; skips nested (depth ≥ 1) and cron requesters; defers session-store reads until the in-memory registry gating passes (this runs on every child settle fleet-wide); reuses `buildChildCompletionFindings` so the wake carries the wave's results; delivers via `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` (active requesters get it steered into the live turn, parked ones get a new origin-routed turn).
- **Trigger seams** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts`): fires from `completeCleanupBookkeeping` (the funnel all cleanup-terminal paths share) and from `suspendPendingFinalDelivery`; the suspended-delivery discard sweep passes `skipRequesterSettleWake` so a 24 h-later discard cannot re-wake. Fire-and-forget — settle bookkeeping never blocks on the wake.
- **Transient-failure retry** (second commit): the settle wake is the only event that ever fires after a drain, so a wake turn lost to a provider stall would re-park the requester permanently (observed live — see Evidence). Bounded recovery: up to 3 attempts with 30 s/120 s backoff, each retry under a fresh `:retry-N` idempotency suffix (the gateway dedupe caches terminal run outcomes per key, so re-dispatching the same key would no-op). A legitimately silent wake reply already classifies as delivered and never retries; terminal failures and an abandoned requester stop immediately.
- **Why source, not a prompt/dist mitigation:** parking is *defined by* no turn running, so prompt-assembly mitigations can only decorate turns that occur — they cannot create the wake turn. A downstream fleet's compiled-dist attempts hit exactly the races resolved here at the source seams (last-sibling detection, give-up/suspension semantics, idempotency).
- **Scope note:** delete-cleanup children leave the registry at settle, so a pure delete-mode fan-out gets partial/no findings in the wake message (the parking class observed in production is keep-mode).
- Release note: fixed top-level sessions parking after parallel subagent fan-outs — the requester is now woken to synthesize when its last child settles, including when a child's completion announce gave up.

target.title: fix(ollama): stop oversized stream records from growing memory
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users connected to a malfunctioning or hostile Ollama endpoint could see OpenClaw memory keep growing when the endpoint streamed an arbitrarily large NDJSON record without a newline.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native Ollama parser now caps each pending NDJSON record at 16 MiB using the original response bytes, resets the count at every newline, and cancels the reader before reporting an overflow. The risk is bounded to individual records larger than 16 MiB; long streams made of valid smaller records remain supported, and this does not change request timeout behavior addressed by #96635.

## User Impact

OpenClaw now stops an oversized Ollama stream record with an actionable error instead of retaining unbounded response data in memory. Normal multi-record Ollama responses continue to stream as before.

## Evidence

AI-assisted.

Premise: Ollama documents streamed REST responses as newline-delimited JSON with the `application/x-ndjson` content type: https://docs.ollama.com/api/streaming. A request timeout does not bound a continuously arriving record that never reaches its newline delimiter.

Real machine / production-path proof used Linux 6.8.0-134-generic x86_64, Node v24.18.0, a real localhost `node:http` server exposing `/api/chat`, and the exported production `createOllamaStreamFn`. The server sent one 20 MiB JSON record in 1 MiB writes. The same temporary harness was run with:

```text
node --import tsx /tmp/ollama-ndjson-real-proof.mts
```

Negative control / before, latest `upstream/main` (`d6fc3d34e2010997d4f67807b30c336347808f31`) in a detached worktree: the client accepted the complete 20,971,644-byte record and returned its `ok` content.

```json
{"node":"v24.18.0","recordBytes":20971644,"bytesWritten":20971645,"responseClosed":true,"terminal":{"type":"done","content":[{"type":"text","text":"ok"}]}}
```

After, commit `296d1e03`: the same production path stopped at the 16 MiB record cap, surfaced the overflow, and closed the live HTTP response before the server finished its payload.

```json
{"node":"v24.18.0","recordBytes":20971644,"bytesWritten":19923066,"responseClosed":true,"terminal":{"type":"error","errorMessage":"Ollama NDJSON record exceeds 16777216 bytes"}}
```

Focused regression and controls:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  106 passed (106)
```

The focused tests prove overflow cancels the reader and that two separate 9 MiB newline-delimited records do not trip a total-stream cap. Targeted oxfmt, oxlint, and `git diff --check` also passed. `autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output` reported no accepted/actionable findings (patch correct, confidence 0.96).

Not tested: a live Ollama daemon/model or remote host; the real HTTP proof uses an Ollama-compatible localhost endpoint so it can deterministically exercise the malformed-record condition without model credentials.

target.title: fix(qqbot): require own account credential entries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQBot logout/setup credential cleanup could treat prototype-inherited named account entries or inherited credential fields as explicit user config. In affected programmatic config shapes, logout could report cleanup for config the user did not own or continue resolving inherited credentials after cleanup skipped the write.

## Why This Change Was Made

QQBot credential cleanup now uses own-property checks across the complete logout/setup account path. Named account resolution, default-account selection, setup updates, bridge resolution, and credential clearing agree that only own `channels.qqbot.accounts.<id>` entries and own `clientSecret` / `clientSecretFile` fields are mutable user config.

Named account objects are normalized to their own enumerable properties before engine and bridge credential resolution, so an owned account entry cannot inherit `appId`, `clientSecret`, or `clientSecretFile` from its prototype.

## User Impact

QQBot logout and setup cleanup now ignore prototype-inherited account data and clear only credentials actually present on the user's config object. Normal owned-account logout still removes `clientSecret` / `clientSecretFile`, retains non-secret fields such as `appId`, and writes the cleaned config through the existing runtime path.

Programmatic configurations that intentionally depend on prototype-inherited QQBot properties will no longer resolve those properties. JSON/JSON5 config files cannot encode prototype inheritance.

target.title: fix: startup recovers from stale npm plugin generations
target.body:
Closes #107841

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with older managed npm plugin generation directories on disk could keep hitting startup "conflicting plugin install metadata" during upgrade or restart when persisted registry metadata pointed at an older plugin generation.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw now treats recorded npm install paths as the freshness boundary for global installed plugins. If the persisted registry points outside the recorded npm generation, startup rebuilds a derived registry from the current install record instead of reusing stale plugin metadata.

This does not delete old generation directories or change npm install cleanup behavior.

## User Impact

Users can restart after managed npm plugin upgrades without manually deleting stale `npm/projects/*__openclaw-generation__*` directories. Current install records remain authoritative, and old generations can remain on disk until normal cleanup handles them.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the stale persisted-registry case with a regression test that writes old and current `@openclaw/whatsapp` managed npm generations and persists metadata rooted at the old generation.
- Before the fix, the regression failed because the snapshot source stayed `persisted` instead of rebuilding as `derived`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/plugin-registry-snapshot.test.ts -t "derives from the recorded npm generation"`: 1 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/plugin-registry-snapshot.test.ts`: 25 passed.

target.title: fix(parallel): resolve env search key refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Parallel web search credential resolution when the configured API key is an env-backed SecretRef. The provider previously used the older strict config string reader, so SecretRef objects did not behave like direct `apiKey` strings or the documented `PARALLEL_API_KEY` fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parallel now uses the shared web-search credential resolver, matching the credential contract used by provider-local web search runtimes: direct configured values win, env SecretRefs resolve from their referenced env var, and the provider env fallback is used only when no credential is configured.

## User Impact

Users can configure `plugins.entries.parallel.config.webSearch.apiKey` as an env SecretRef without needing a live key in config. Missing or unsupported SecretRefs fail closed instead of silently falling back to an unrelated ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY` value.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 35 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude` reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- Default Codex autoreview was attempted first but the local OpenAI API key is rejected with 401, so it could not produce a review.

## Proof

- Added dispatch-level coverage through `createParallelWebSearchProvider().createTool(...).execute(...)`, lazy runtime loading, plugin-owned `plugins.entries.parallel.config.webSearch.apiKey`, scoped config merge, and the mocked trusted endpoint request.
- The resolved env SecretRef test proves the actual request header `x-api-key` is the configured env ref value and not the ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY` fallback.
- The unavailable env SecretRef test sets ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY`, configures a missing env SecretRef, expects `missing_parallel_api_key`, and proves zero endpoint calls were made.
- Resolver-level coverage remains for direct configured keys, documented env fallback, default/custom env SecretRefs, and unavailable/unsupported SecretRefs.
- No `PARALLEL_API_KEY` is available in this environment. A local loopback HTTP proof attempt was intentionally blocked by OpenClaw's trusted web-search SSRF guard, so no fake local endpoint was used as live Parallel proof.

target.title: fix(kill-tree): verify process group leader before using group kill to prevent gateway SIGTERM (#76259)
target.body:
## PR #94697 — Risk Closure Supplement > **Status: ClawSweeper P1/P2 items addressed** ### What changed since v1 (post ClawSweeper review) | Version | Change | Closes | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | | v1 (commit 9fd6116) | Initial leader-check + `detached:true` override | #76259 main case | | v2 (commit 3b261a9) | Propagate `detached:true` through 6 caller sites | ClawSweeper P1 — detached descendant cleanup | | v3 (commit cede936) | Propagate `detached:true` to agent-core NodeExecutionEnv | ClawSweeper P1 — full caller audit | | v4 (commit 7fb01ea) | (a) 4 new fail-safe tests for ps failure modes
(b) `/proc//stat` Linux fallback
(c) Source-level caller audit table | ClawSweeper P1 availability + P2 validation | --- ### ClawSweeper items — closed #### [P1] Compatibility — shared omitted-option Unix cleanup now depends on ps **Status: closed by /proc fallback + fail-safe tests.** The shared `killProcessTree(pid)` path (omitted `detached`) calls `isProcessGroupLeader(pid)`, which now has two layers: 1. **Primary**: `ps -p -o pgid=` (works on macOS, Linux, FreeBSD) 2. **Secondary** (Linux only): `/proc//stat` field 5 (pgid) — works on distroless / scratch / minimal Alpine where `ps` is absent 3. **Tertiary fail-safe**: both fail → returns `false` → single-pid kill (no group kill, no gateway SIGTERM) The fail-safe path is now covered by 4 new tests in `kill-tree.test.ts`: - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps throws - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps exits non-zero - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps stdout is non-numeric - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps stdout is empty Worst-case behavior on a Linux image without `ps` and without `/proc` (extremely rare — e.g. chroot without procfs): single-pid kill is used. This is **strictly safer than the pre-PR main**, which would have done `process.kill(-pid, ...)` unconditionally and SIGTERM'd the gateway. #### [P1] Availability — detached descendant cleanup after leader exit **Status: closed by v2 caller audit.** The P1 scenario (detached leader exits → `isProcessGroupLeader` returns false → descendants orphaned) is closed by **all 6 detached-spawn callers now explicitly passing `detached: true`** to `killProcessTree` / `signalProcessTree`. The `detached: true` short-circuits the leader check (`opts?.detached === true || ...`), preserving group kill unconditionally. #### Caller audit table (source-level proof) | Caller file | Spawn line | Spawn `detached` value | Cleanup call site | Passes `detached: true`? | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------ | | `packages/agent-core/src/harness/env/nodejs.ts` (NodeExecutionEnv.exec) | L319, L321 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L298 (abort), L339 (timeout) | ✅ | | `packages/agent-core/src/harness/env/nodejs.ts` (runCommand helper) | L152 | **not set** (attached) | L162 | ✅ correctly **omitted** | | `src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.ts` | L63, L65 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L130, L134 | ✅ | | `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts` | L83, L87 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L246 | ✅ | | `src/agents/shell-snapshot.ts` | L445, L447 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L460, L464 | ✅ | | `src/agents/sessions/tools/bash.ts` | L63, L65 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L77, L87 | ✅ | | `src/process/exec.ts` (runCommandWithTimeout) | L396, L402 | `killProcessTree && process.platform !== "win32"` (conditional) | L501 (inside `if (killProcessTree)` guard) | ✅ | **Invariant**: every caller that spawns with `detached: true` passes `detached: true` to cleanup; every caller that spawns attached passes nothing (or `detached: false`). The two cannot drift because they share the same `killProcessTree` option flag at the spawn site. #### [P2] Persistent data-model change detected in `src/agents/sessions/tools/bash.ts` **Status: false positive — no serialized state change.** The only change to `bash.ts` is on L77 and L87, where the existing `killProcessTree(child.pid)` call gains a second argument `{ detached: true }`. This is a function-call argument change, not a structural change to any persisted type. No `SessionState`, `BashSnapshot`, or serialized payload is touched. The `KillProcessTreeOptions` type itself was already extended with `detached?: boolean` in PR #71681; this PR only consumes the existing field. #### [P2] Run current-head process cleanup validation before merge **Status: closed by validation script.** Ran the exact [P1] acceptance criteria commands from ClawSweeper's review: ```bash # 1. kill-tree unit tests node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/kill-tree.test.ts # 2. agent cleanup paths node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.test.ts \ src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts # 3. exec / shell / bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/shell-snapshot.test.ts \ src/process/exec.test.ts ``` Real process-group behavior verified on macOS arm64 (Sequoia): - **Step A**: attached child → `isProcessGroupLeader? false` → single-pid kill used (expected) - **Step B**: detached child → `isProcessGroupLeader? true` → group kill reaches descendants (expected) --- ### Merge readiness - ✅ All ClawSweeper P1 items closed with source-level evidence - ✅ All ClawSweeper P2 items closed (false positive explained + validation run) - ✅ Test count: 19/19 (15 original + 4 fail-safe = 19) - ✅ No API change to `KillProcessTreeOptions` (existing `detached?: boolean` field) - ✅ No new runtime dependency (only `node:fs` for /proc fallback) - ✅ Backwards compatible: pre-PR main callers that omit `detached` see safer behavior (no gateway SIGTERM risk); callers that spawn detached and pass `detached: true` see identical behavior to pre-#71681 main - ✅ Windows path untouched --- **Ready for maintainer review.** --- ## Summary What problem does this PR solve? - `killProcessTree` on Unix defaults `useGroupKill` to `true` when callers omit `{ detached: false }`. If the PID is not its own process group leader, `process.kill(-pid, ...)` targets whatever process group `pid` belongs to — typically the gateway's own process group, causing the gateway to receive SIGTERM. Why does this matter now? - #71681 made the fix opt-in (callers must pass `{ detached: false }`), but any caller that omits the option still triggers the bug. On macOS with launchd-managed gateway, a non-detached child that becomes a zombie triggers `killProcessTree` → `process.kill(-pid, SIGTERM)` → gateway receives SIGTERM and exits. What is the intended outcome? - `killProcessTree` verifies whether the PID is its own process group leader via `ps -p -o pgid=` before using group kill. Non-leader PIDs fall back to single-pid kill, preventing accidental gateway signaling. - When the caller explicitly passes `detached: true`, group kill is used unconditionally (bypassing the leader check), preserving the ability to clean up detached process groups even after the group leader has exited. What is intentionally out of scope? - Windows behavior is unchanged (taskkill /T already handles tree termination correctly). The `detached: false` option is preserved as an explicit caller override. What does success look like? - All 15 vitest tests pass (10 original + 3 original new + 2 new for detached:true override). A non-group-leader PID receives single-pid kill while a group leader PID still receives group kill. A detached:true call forces group kill even after leader exit. What should reviewers focus on? - Whether `isProcessGroupLeader` using `spawnSync("ps", ...)` is acceptable for the kill path (it's not a hot path), and whether the 500ms timeout is appropriate. - The `detached:true` override added for the P1 fix in #94697 review. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? Closes #76259 Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? - Related #71662 (original issue) - Related #71681 (original opt-in fix) - ClawSweeper review #94697 (P1: preserve detached group cleanup after leader exit) Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? Reporter issue with numbered repro and suggested fix; ClawSweeper queueable-fix criteria in comments. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) **Behavior or issue addressed:** `killProcessTree` group-kill defaults to `true` and can SIGTERM the gateway when the PID is not a process group leader. After leader exit, `isProcessGroupLeader` returns false, but `detached:true` forces group kill. **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64 (Sequoia), local checkout, branch `fix/76259-kill-tree-group-leader` **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** ```bash # Run validation script node scripts/validate-94697.mjs # Test process group behavior manually: # 1. Spawn attached child - shares parent's PG (non-leader) node -e "const {spawn}=require('child_process'); const c=spawn('sleep',['60'],{stdio:['ignore','pipe','pipe']}); console.log('attached PID',c.pid);" # 2. Spawn detached child - becomes own group leader node -e "const {spawn}=require('child_process'); const c=spawn('sleep',['60'],{stdio:['ignore','pipe','pipe'],detached:true}); c.unref(); console.log('detached PID',c.pid);" ``` **Evidence after fix:** ``` ============================================================ 1. Unit tests (kill-tree) — platform=darwin ============================================================ ✅ PASS ============================================================ 2. Agent cleanup paths ============================================================ ✅ PASS ============================================================ 3. Exec/shell/bash ============================================================ ✅ PASS ============================================================ 4. Real process-group behavior proof (platform=darwin) ============================================================ ── Step A: attached child shares parent's PG (non-leader) ── child PID=11673 isProcessGroupLeader? false (expected: false on attached child) ── Step B: detached child becomes its own group leader ── child PID=11685 isProcessGroupLeader? true (expected: true) group kill via process.kill(-pid) issued ============================================================ SUMMARY ============================================================ Unit tests (kill-tree): PASS Unit tests (agent cleanup): PASS Unit tests (exec/shell/bash): PASS Overall: ✅ ALL GREEN ``` **Observed result after fix:** - attached child (non-leader): `isProcessGroupLeader` returns `false` → single-pid kill used ✅ - detached child (leader): `isProcessGroupLeader` returns `true` → group kill reaches descendants ✅ - All 19 unit tests pass ✅

target.title: fix(qqbot): add timeouts to API response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQBot API calls could still hang forever after response headers arrived if the response body stalled. Users sending messages or reading QQBot API responses could see the request remain pending even though the existing header-phase timeout had already been cleared.

## Why This Change Was Made

The QQBot API client now keeps the request deadline alive until the response body has been read or released. The existing caller signal, SSRF guard, response release cleanup, upload behavior, and API error shaping are preserved.

## User Impact

QQBot API calls now fail quickly with a timeout when the provider stops streaming a response body, instead of leaving the send/API path stuck indefinitely. Normal successful responses keep the same behavior.

## Evidence

Base: upstream/main `3ec2a50d6c0a62a484e630536c658a8357e4e211`
Head: `1f6ea53af2` (`fix(qqbot): add timeouts to API response reads`)

Controlled HTTP proof after the response-read deadline change:

```json

  "proof": "qqbot-api-response-body-timeout",
  "baseUrl": "http://198.18.0.1:44379",
  "timeoutMs": 500,
  "elapsedMs": 518,

  "headersSent": true,
  "bodyStarted": true,
  "serverSawClose": true,

}
```

target.title: fix(skills): preserve emoji in long history scans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Skill Workshop history scanning could produce malformed provider-bound transcript text when its per-session cap split an emoji or another supplementary character in the retained prefix, head, or tail.

## Why This Change Was Made

The downstream history-scan cap now uses the normalization core's UTF-16-safe prefix and slice helpers while preserving the existing budget, omission marker, redaction order, and head/tail layout. This is distinct from #106370, which addresses the earlier 60,000-character experience-review formatter cap; this change covers the later 16,000-character per-session history-scan cap.

## User Impact

Skill history scans now send well-formed Unicode transcripts at every truncation boundary without increasing their context budget.

## Evidence

- AI-assisted: yes. The truncation branches and downstream history-scan path were reviewed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/history-scan.test.ts -t 'keeps .* UTF-16 safe'` - 3/3 tests passed; 23 skipped.
- Tests cover the prefix-only budget and retained head and tail boundaries.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` - passed.
- Focused validation used the local fallback because Blacksmith Testbox was unavailable and sanitized AWS Crabbox could not acquire a lease.
- Initial CI run [29359504345](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29359504345) completed. Selected build, type, contract, QA smoke, and test lanes passed. The three failing source checks reproduce only current-base debt outside this PR: an unused Bonjour export, a stale QA Lab max-lines baseline entry, and two over-limit system-agent files.

target.title: fix(anthropic): read claudeCodeVersion at runtime to prevent stale user-agent bearer auth failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Anthropic OAuth requests carry a hardcoded `claudeCodeVersion = "2.1.75"` user-agent string in two places:

| File | Symbol | Code path |
|---|---|---|
| `src/llm/providers/anthropic.ts` | `claudeCodeVersion` | Legacy SDK provider (OAuth bearer) |
| `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts` | `CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION` | Managed Anthropic transport (native SSE) |

When the installed `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` CLI is any version other than `2.1.75`, every OAuth-authenticated request still declares itself as `2.1.75`. The Anthropic backend can reject the mismatched version, and bearer auth fails. This is issue #94716, confirmed still reproducible on current `main` (the constant is still hardcoded at `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` post file-move).

## Changes

### `src/llm/utils/claude-code-version.ts` (new)

Single source of truth, resolved **per call** via an injectable resolver:

```typescript
export type ClaudeCodeVersionResolver = () => string | null;

// Reads @anthropic-ai/claude-code/package.json at call time.
// Uses createRequire(import.meta.url) — no execSync, no module-load caching.
export const defaultClaudeCodeVersionResolver: ClaudeCodeVersionResolver = () => { … };

let resolver: ClaudeCodeVersionResolver = defaultClaudeCodeVersionResolver;
export function __setClaudeCodeVersionResolver(next: ClaudeCodeVersionResolver): void { … }
export function __resetClaudeCodeVersionResolver(): void { … }

export function resolveClaudeCodeVersion(): string { … }   // throws on any failure

// Called at client-construction time in both providers.
export function claudeCodeUserAgent(): string {
  return `claude-cli/${resolveClaudeCodeVersion()}`;
}
```

Design points:
- **Per-call resolution.** `claudeCodeUserAgent()` calls `resolveClaudeCodeVersion()` on every invocation. No module-load constant; a package upgrade takes effect without a runtime restart.
- **Injectable resolver.** `__setClaudeCodeVersionResolver` / `__resetClaudeCodeVersionResolver` let tests run without the host package in the module graph.
- **Fail loudly, never silently.** Null / empty / non-digit-leading / non-string / throw → exception. No fallback to a stale version — a silent fallback to the old hardcoded constant would reproduce the exact bug this PR fixes, just with a smaller window.
- **Scoped package name.** `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` — not unscoped `claude` — prevents unofficial package resolution into an OAuth identity header.

### `src/llm/providers/anthropic.ts` / `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts`

Remove the hardcoded version constants. Import and call `claudeCodeUserAgent()` in `defaultHeaders`.

### `src/llm/utils/claude-code-version.test.ts` (new)

9 deterministic unit tests via resolver injection (no host package required in CI):

| # | Test | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | resolver returns `"2.1.177"` | `resolveClaudeCodeVersion()` → `"2.1.177"` |
| 2 | resolver returns `null` | throws `/invalid value.*null/` |
| 3 | resolver returns `""` | throws `/invalid value/` |
| 4 | resolver returns `"not-a-version"` | throws `/invalid value/` |
| 5 | resolver returns `123` | throws `/invalid value/` |
| 6 | resolver throws | rethrows with `/Failed to resolve/` wrapping cause |
| 7 | resolver returns `"2.0.0-beta"` (digit-leading) | accepted as-is |
| 8 | `claudeCodeUserAgent()` reads active resolver | header matches injected version |
| 9 | resolver fails → `claudeCodeUserAgent()` throws | no stale fallback (regression for #94716) |

## Evidence

```
vitest run src/llm/utils/claude-code-version.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  9 passed (9)

tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck: exit 0

node scripts/proof-claudeCodeVersion.mjs
  user-agent: claude-cli/2.1.177  ← installed @anthropic-ai/claude-code (matches host CLI, not the old "2.1.75" constant)
```

Full wire capture (OpenClaw → capture server showing `user-agent: claude-cli/2.1.177` in request headers) requires a dist build from this branch and is available on request.

## Known open items (tracked, in progress on this branch)

- **Rebase required.** `src/llm/providers/anthropic.ts` moved to `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` on current `main`; this branch predates the move and needs to retarget both provider files.
- **Lint:** `no-underscore-dangle` flags the `__setClaudeCodeVersionResolver` / `__resetClaudeCodeVersionResolver` test-injection helpers — needs a rename or scoped disable comment.
- **Pre-existing test regression uncovered during review:** 5 tests in the existing `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` (not the new file added by this PR) fail against this branch — being root-caused and fixed rather than skipped, since a silent skip would hide whatever the actual interaction is.

None of the above changes the design or the root-cause fix above; they're mechanical follow-up commits on this same branch.

## Related

There's a second open PR for the same issue, #95265, using a module-load-cached resolver with a silent fallback to the old `"2.1.75"` constant on resolution failure. Commented on that PR with the specific design tradeoffs — the short version is that a silent fallback to the stale constant reproduces the bug class this fix exists to close. Happy to consolidate with maintainer input.

Fixes #94716.

target.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded after-compaction hooks needed a safe way to request a fresh session after compaction, but the first version exposed the gateway reset service directly from inside the hook. That was unsafe in two ways: it awaited reset while the active embedded run was still executing the hook, which could make the reset service abort and wait on its own run, and it let hook code pass any session key instead of being bound to the current hook session.

This PR fixes the OpenClaw core lifecycle boundary by making `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)` current-session scoped and deferred. Hook code can request `"new"` or `"reset"`, but it cannot name another session. The owning embedded-run or compaction lifecycle drains the queued request after hook dispatch / run execution has exited.

## Summary

- Replaces the proposed arbitrary-key hook reset API with a current-session-scoped `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)` request.
- Defers hook-requested resets until the owning lifecycle has left hook dispatch / embedded-run execution, avoiding the active-run self-wait path in the gateway reset service.
- Wires the deferred reset queue through run-level hooks, direct compaction after-hooks, and queued/context-engine-owned after-compaction hooks.
- Adds regression coverage for deferred execution, current-session binding, and overflow compaction hook API availability.

## Hatched Egg / Behavior Evidence

This is an OpenClaw core lifecycle fix, not a Remnic property-data fix. Remnic/context compaction exposed the symptom, but the bug was in the embedded-agent hook/session reset boundary.

Before this revision, the hook API called `performGatewaySessionReset(...)` synchronously from inside an awaited hook and accepted a caller-supplied key. That could make an after-compaction hook abort and wait on its own active embedded run, and it allowed a hook for one session to target another session key.

After this revision:

```ts
await hookContext.api.resetSession("new")
expect(performGatewaySessionResetMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
```

The hook call only queues the current session reset while hook code is still executing. The lifecycle owner later drains the queue with trusted metadata:

```ts
expect(performGatewaySessionResetMock).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
  key: "agent:main:session-1",
  agentId: "main",
  reason: "new",
  commandSource: "embedded-agent:hook",
})
```

Cross-session targeting is no longer part of the API. The regression test also proves a string that used to be interpreted as an arbitrary session key is rejected as an invalid reason:

```ts
await expect(
  hookContext.api.resetSession("agent:other-session" as "reset"),
).rejects.toThrow(/reason "new" or "reset"/)
```

## Evidence / Validation

Rebased onto `origin/main` at `774cd25aa61` and pushed as `1b28ea41a9c`.

```text
$ node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-embedded-agent.config.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts

Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       175 passed (175)
```

```text
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-pr-compaction-hook-api.tsbuildinfo
# passed
```

```text
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-agents-pr-compaction-hook-api.tsbuildinfo
# passed
```

```text
$ git diff --check
# passed
```

target.title: fix(gateway): regenerate native hook descriptors when relay unavailable after restart
target.body:
## Summary

Native hook descriptors were not regenerated when the relay was unavailable during gateway restart, causing hooks to silently fail until manual intervention. Falls through to normal OpenClaw policy evaluation instead of hard-blocking when the relay is unavailable.

## Linked context

Closes #89325

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Native hooks silently failing after gateway restart with unavailable relay
- Real environment tested: Codex app-server with native hook relay (unit/integration tests)
- Exact steps or command run after this patch (rebased onto origin/main, 2026-07-16):
```
vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts \
    src/cli/native-hook-relay-cli.test.ts
```
- Evidence after fix: CLI-level native hook tests pass; fallthrough behavior confirmed
- Observed result after fix: Relay unavailability triggers fallthrough to policy evaluation instead of hard-block
- Rebase status: Rebased onto latest origin/main (fdd1acb3285), no conflicts
- What was not tested: Live relay restart cycle on real Codex harness
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: Relay lifecycle testing requires live Codex; unit tests cover the code path

## Tests and validation

- Commands: `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts`
- Regression coverage: approval-bridge.test.ts covers both error and fallthrough paths
- Before: Relay unavailable at restart → native hook descriptors not regenerated → hooks silently fail
- After: Relay becomes available → descriptors regenerated → hooks work without manual intervention

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? Yes — failed relay no longer hard-blocks approval
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? Yes — fallthrough changes approval path
- What is the highest-risk area? Security boundary: falling through to policy evaluation instead of hard-blocking
- How is that risk mitigated? The before_tool_call hook path enforces the same policy; no policy gap introduced

target.title: fix(ai): normalize non-conforming tool-call ids reaching Anthropic/Google targets (#95623)
target.body:
Fixes #95623

## What Problem This Solves

After a cross-provider failover, an OpenAI-responses composite tool-call id (`call_XXX|fc_YYY`) can reach an **Anthropic** target still containing the `|`. Anthropic requires tool ids matching `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`, so it hard-400s the whole replay and the session is bricked for its own primary provider — no new turns without a reset.

This happens on two paths that the existing `#61254` sanitizer misses:
- **Orphaned tool result** — the paired tool call was dropped (compaction/windowing), so there is no in-pass map entry and the raw id passes through untouched.
- **Same-model-tagged call** — a failover-introduced id whose provenance looks same-model as the Anthropic target skips normalization (`!isSameModel` guard), so both the call and its result keep the `|`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`packages/ai/src/providers/transform-messages.ts` owns cross-provider tool-call-id normalization but only normalized `toolCall` ids when `!isSameModel`, and `toolResult` ids only via an in-pass `toolCallIdMap`. Non-conforming ids leaked through both gaps.

A blanket "always normalize" is unsafe: the OpenAI-completions/OpenAI-responses/Mistral normalizers are **not idempotent** on their own native ids (openai-completions strips the `|fc_…` half; openai-responses reads the `source` message; mistral is a stateful id map), so applying them to same-model native ids would corrupt valid replays.

So `transformMessages` gains an opt-in `targetSafeToolCallIds` flag, passed `true` only by the **Anthropic and Google** call sites whose normalizers are charset scrubs that are idempotent on their native ids. In target-safe mode every tool id reaching the target is normalized — the same-model call and the map-miss result included — and because the scrub is deterministic, a call and its result stay paired. Every other provider keeps the default (`false`), so their behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

The shared transform owns this invariant, so the fix stays there (not at the Anthropic transport-serialization boundary, which cannot see the shared call/result pairing). Non-goals: no change to any provider's normalizer semantics, no change to cross-provider behavior, and no id-collision hashing.

## User Impact

Sessions that fail over to an OpenAI-responses model and later replay to an Anthropic primary no longer brick on an Anthropic 400 — the foreign composite id is scrubbed to a conforming id (`call_XXX_fc_YYY`) on both the call and its result. Google targets get the same protection. OpenAI/Mistral users are unaffected.

## Evidence

Real behavior via the actual `transformMessages` (Anthropic target, composite id `call_AbCd0123|fc_beef01`), head `e7e315d6c5a3`:

~~~text
AFTER S1-safe orphan (targetSafe=true):          ["result:call_AbCd0123_fc_beef01"]                                | PIPE-SURVIVES=false
AFTER S3-safe same-model-mistag (targetSafe=true): ["call:call_AbCd0123_fc_beef01","result:call_AbCd0123_fc_beef01"] | PIPE-SURVIVES=false
REGRESSION default (targetSafe=false) same-model:  ["call:call_AbCd0123|fc_beef01","result:call_AbCd0123|fc_beef01"] | PIPE-SURVIVES=true
~~~

The two target-safe paths scrub the `|`; the default path leaves a same-model id byte-for-byte untouched (proving no OpenAI/Mistral corruption). On current `main` (target-safe absent) both S1 and S3 leak — `PIPE-SURVIVES=true`.

- `vitest run packages/ai/src/providers/transform-messages.test.ts` — 5 passed (2 red-first #95623 guards for S1/S3 + 3 regressions: default-mode composite untouched, cross-provider pair still mapped, source-requiring normalizer never invoked on a map-miss result).
- Negative control: with the source fix stashed, the S1 & S3 guard tests fail (`expected 'call_AbCd0123|fc_beef01' to be 'call_AbCd0123_fc_beef01'`) — confirms the tests guard the bug.
- Broader regression: all `packages/ai/src/providers` tests — 356 passed; the 1 failure (`openai-chatgpt-responses` zstd-SSE encoding) reproduces identically with my change stashed, i.e. pre-existing/unrelated (a zstd env issue on this host).
- `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` / `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` — no errors; `oxfmt --check` — clean; `check:loc` — passes (all growth in the sub-500-line transform; the three oversized provider files stay net-zero).

## Notes

- Distinct from #95671 (guarded only the same-model path at the transport-serialization boundary, missing orphan results) and #95629 — this fixes both leak paths at the owning transform boundary with zero cross-provider regression.
- AI-assisted (Claude Code); I have reviewed and understand every line.

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Some deployments serve a Claude/MiniMax model through a proxy that intermittently degrades a native `tool_use` block into plain text. In that degraded case the tool call arrives as the namespaced/bare XML attribute dialect — `<invoke name="tool"><parameter name="x">v</parameter></invoke>`, optionally wrapped in `<function_calls>...</function_calls>` and optionally prefixed with `antml:` or `mm:`.

On current `main` two gaps remained:

1. The visible-text sanitizer recognized the `antml:` prefix but not the `mm:` prefix, so a degraded `mm:invoke` block leaked verbatim into the user-visible reply.
2. The persist-path stripper (`packages/tool-call-repair` `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks`) did not recognize the attribute-dialect invoke at all, so an unfenced standalone degraded invoke block was written into the durable `done.message` instead of being scrubbed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user, and it must not be persisted into session state either — but a legitimate code example of the same markup (inside a fenced or inline code span) must be preserved, not deleted. This change teaches both layers about the full attribute dialect using a closed `(?:antml:|mm:)?` namespace allow-list, so arbitrary `ns:` tokens in prose are never matched.

This PR was re-implemented on top of current `main` after upstream refactored the tool-call-repair package (the new `scanXmlishToolCall` seam and code-region helpers). The change is scoped to the net delta that still reproduces on `main`:

- **Visible text** (`assistant-visible-text.ts`): mirror the existing `antml:` handling for the `mm:` namespace in the tag-name scan, quick-check, and payload-start patterns. The `<function_calls>`-wrapped bare-invoke case is already scrubbed by the package strip stage in the delivery pipeline.
- **Persist path** (`packages/tool-call-repair`): a dedicated linear scanner recognizes a complete standalone invoke block (bare/`antml:`/`mm:`, `<function_calls>` wrapper, self-closing, and zero-parameter forms). The scanner returns `none`/`incomplete`/`complete`, so on an unterminated open the strip loop bails and preserves the remainder — exactly mirroring the existing dialects — keeping the scan linear on adversarial input.
- **Code-region awareness**: the strip takes an optional code-region predicate evaluated at the block's start offset. Fenced/inline Markdown examples of the invoke dialect are preserved while unfenced standalone leaked blocks are scrubbed. Without a predicate the package strip lazily computes code regions so a bare call still spares examples.
- **Plugin SDK contract preserved**: the exported `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it forces a scrub of every region, even inside code, for untrusted callers), with code-aware behavior available only via the explicit `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` opt-in.
- **Layering**: `findCodeRegions`/`isInsideCode`/`CodeRegion` were moved into `normalization-core` (the package's only dependency) so `tool-call-repair` can share one implementation without importing app source; `src/shared/text/code-regions.ts` re-exports them so existing callers are unaffected.

Non-goals/boundaries: the native Anthropic/DSML transports are untouched; no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced; the equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged; the invoke dialect is recognized only by the strip/sanitize paths (never promoted to an executable call and never wired into the stream-buffering scanner).

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude/MiniMax routes no longer see raw namespaced/bare `invoke` tool-call XML in their replies, and the leaked block is no longer written into the persisted message (no session-state content loss). Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped. A resolved-review audit also removed an O(n²) worst case on the persist strip path, so adversarial degraded text cannot cause pathological CPU use.

## Evidence

Focused regression tests were added at the layers that own the contract:
- `packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.test.ts`: invoke-dialect variants (bare/`antml:`/`mm:`, `function_calls` wrapper, self-closing, zero-param), code-region preservation vs. unfenced scrub, the predicate override, and a linear-time guard against many unterminated opens.
- `src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts`: the `preserveCodeRegions` opt-in and strict default.

```

A2 mm-visible       => "Working on it.\n<mm:invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<mm:parameter name=\"city\">Paris</mm:parameter>\n</mm:invoke>"
A3 bare-fc-visible  => "Done.\n<function_calls>\n<invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<parameter name=\"city\">Paris</parameter>\n</invoke>\n</function_calls>"

=== AFTER (this branch) ===

A3 bare-fc-visible  => "Done."
C1 persist-unfenced => "Here you go.\n"
B1 persist-fenced   => "...```xml\n<invoke ...>...\n```..."   (still preserved)
B2 persist-inline   => "Use the `<invoke name=\"get_weather\">` opener to start."   (still preserved)
```

target.title: fix(agents): deliver the sessions_yield message instead of a silent spawn-and-wait turn
target.body:
Fixes #107788

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users asking a question that the agent delegates to a background subagent (`sessions_spawn` + `sessions_yield` with an interim message like "Research started — I'll send the results shortly") would see nothing at all: the yield acknowledgment was never delivered, and the chat stayed silent for minutes until the subagent's announce arrived. The model believes the ack was shown (the tool result echoes it), so it never re-sends it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The yield `message` died in two places: the embedded runner persisted it only as a hidden (`display: false`) context message (`attempt.sessions-yield.ts:persistSessionsYieldContextMessage`), and the Codex app-server wrapper dropped the string entirely (`onYieldDetected` took no argument). Neither harness carried it into the run result, so the reply pipeline's empty-payload exit (`agent-runner.ts`) returned silence.

Following the triage's recommended shape: both harnesses now carry an optional `yieldMessage` as an attempt-result fact next to the existing `yieldDetected`/`meta.yielded` boolean, and the canonical reply pipeline emits it once — only when the turn yielded, is interactive (external-user provenance; subagent runs and heartbeats stay silent), and produced no other user-visible delivery. The reply runner owns the "what to deliver for an empty run" semantic (it already synthesizes the empty-interactive fallback there); this PR adds the yield case beside it and leaves announce semantics, yield context persistence, and fence/admission behavior intact.

One subtlety the delivery guard must get right: `hasVisibleOutboundDeliveryEvidence`/`hasCompletedTerminalDeliveryEvidence` count **accepted session spawns** and cron adds as delivery evidence (replay-safety semantics, not user visibility). A spawn-and-yield turn always has an accepted spawn, so gating the ack on those helpers makes the fix a no-op in exactly the reported scenario — the live-gateway run below demonstrates this. The ack therefore gates only on strictly user-visible evidence (streamed terminal blocks, source replies, visible message-tool sends, approval prompts). This is also the material difference from #108540, whose `hasVisibleDelivery` gate includes `successfulSideEffectDelivery`/`successfulTerminalDelivery` (both spawn-contaminated) and whose regression test mocks the yielded turn without `acceptedSessionSpawns`.

Non-goals: no change to the hidden yield context message, subagent announce delivery, heartbeat semantics, or any config/env surface; the new meta field is additive and consumed per attempt (no registry, no cache).

## User Impact

When an agent spawns background work and yields with a message, that message now reaches the user immediately as a normal reply (chunking/threading/dedupe apply). Spawn-and-yield turns no longer look like delivery failures.

## Evidence

Real behavior — gateway + qa-channel + mock-openai provider driving the exact reported flow (inbound DM → `sessions_spawn` → `sessions_yield` with message → zero assistant payloads), fresh dist build for each run:

Before (current main, head `6f22ef08a37`): the ack wait times out — silence until the subagent announce.
~~~text
### Yield ack delivery proof
- Status: fail
- Details: timed out after 90000ms
  - [ ] yield ack is delivered to the QA DM
~~~

After (this branch): the yield message is delivered as an outbound DM reply.
~~~text
### Yield ack delivery proof
- Status: pass
  - [x] yield ack is delivered to the QA DM
    - Details: ack="Waiting for QA-SUBAGENT-DIRECT-FALLBACK-OK." outbound=qa-dm-yield-ack:Waiting for QA-SUBAGENT-DIRECT-FALLBACK-OK.
~~~

The pre-existing `subagent-completion-direct-fallback` scenario still passes on this branch (completion delivery unchanged).

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — 77 passed, including the new symptom test (yielded spawn turn with `acceptedSessionSpawns` delivers the ack; without a message it stays silent)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts` — 9 passed (guard matrix: heartbeat / non-interactive / silent-expected / message-tool-only / already-delivered / empty message)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts` — 50 passed, including the new Codex `onYield` message passthrough test
- Negative control on unpatched tree: the symptom test fails (`expected reply result to be an object` — the turn returns silence) → the regression tests guard this bug
- `CI=1 pnpm check:changed` — all lanes green except the format lane, which aborts on this Windows host with `spawn ENAMETOOLONG` (file-list length, not a formatting error); `oxfmt --check` on all 14 touched files: "All matched files use the correct format." `oxlint` on touched files: clean. `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json`: no new errors (4 pre-existing environment errors reproduce identically on clean main).

AI-assisted (Claude Code); I have reviewed and understand every line.

target.title: chore(ui): add mock chat fixtures for design QA
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI mock has limited curated chat state for design QA, so reviewers have to rely on ad hoc sessions when checking empty chat, longer transcripts, markdown rendering, code blocks, tables, warnings, and recoverable error copy.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR adds stable dev/mock-only fixture sessions to the Control UI mock server. The proposed fixtures cover a New session empty state, a coding session, a response-shape showcase, and a markdown showcase without changing production gateway or session APIs.

## User Impact

There is no production user-facing behavior change. Developers and designers can load stable mock chat sessions for future Control UI visual review.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 scripts/control-ui-mock-dev.ts`
- `pnpm dev:ui:mock -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5197`
- Browser smoke loaded these proposed mock routes and confirmed the expected fixture content:
  - `/chat?session=agent%3Aopenclaw-mock%3Anew-session`
  - `/chat?session=agent%3Aopenclaw-mock%3Aqa-coding-session`
  - `/chat?session=agent%3Aopenclaw-mock%3Aresponse-shape-showcase`
  - `/chat?session=agent%3Aopenclaw-mock%3Amarkdown-showcase`

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:
  memory . 105/105 files . 933 chunks
```

```
$ openclaw memory index
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
Memory index updated (main).
```

```
$ openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
0.812 memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md:1-9
    Recursive memory search proof.
    Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
    This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
    to verify that nested dated memory files are indexed and searchable
    by the runtime.

0.450 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md:1-6
0.432 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/pr-draft.md:1-32
```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```
$ node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs
=== schema.help.ts: FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch'] ===
Vector search over MEMORY.md and memory/**/*.md (per-agent overrides supported).

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search + memory_get }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts; then use memory_get to pull only the needed lines. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search only }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts and answer from the matching results. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== extensions/memory-core/index.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 127      description:
 128        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 139      description:
 140        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",

=== extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 240      description:
 241        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 410      description:
 411        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",
```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. (c) The two `memory_search` / `memory_get` description strings in `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` are inline string literals; the after-patch lines printed from this branch show the new wording in place. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerates baseline cleanly (no other drift)
- [x] Nested memory smoke search on installed `2026.5.20` returns the new nested file at score `0.812`
- [x] On-branch runtime import shows `FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch']`, `buildPromptSection(...)` output, and `memory_search` / `memory_get` description literals all carry `memory/**/*.md`
- [ ] CI: lint / type / config-baseline check

target.title: fix(web): apply Control UI text size to content typography
target.body:
## Summary

In this PR, the Appearance text-size setting applies across Control UI content typography instead of only affecting the chat transcript. Shared content font sizes now route through `--control-ui-text-scale`, while touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing 16px minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not reintroduce mobile Safari focus zoom.

## Screenshots

Settings at the default M text size, showing the Appearance text-size control in English.

![Settings text size at M](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-settings-text-size-m-en.png)

Overview at XXL text size, showing the larger page typography across cards and form controls.

![Overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-overview-xxl-en.png)

Channels at XXL text size, showing the larger channel cards and actions.

![Channels using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-channels-xxl-en.png)

Mobile Overview at XXL text size, showing the narrow layout with scaled content typography.

![Mobile overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-mobile-overview-xxl-en.png)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Appearance text-size setting so it affects Control UI content typography beyond the chat transcript. Before this PR, the setting could be saved while many Settings, quick settings, overview, channel, session, skill, and content surfaces still used fixed font sizes.

## Why This Change Was Made

In this PR, shared Control UI font sizes route through the existing `--control-ui-text-scale` value instead of hard-coded pixel sizes. The change keeps layout chrome and spacing stable while letting readable content, forms, cards, chat text, composer text, and page typography respond to S/M/L/XL/XXL.

Touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing `--control-ui-input-text-size` minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not shrink mobile inputs below 16px and reintroduce Safari focus zoom.

## User Impact

Changing Text size in Appearance now produces visible typography changes across the main product surfaces, while M remains the normal/default size.

## Validation

target.title: fix(ci): skip Periphery scans for unrelated PR changes
target.body:
Related: #106090
Observed on: #106789

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where pull requests unrelated to iOS, macOS, or shared OpenClawKit could run Periphery scans when `main` advanced after the pull-request event was created. The stale event base SHA made base-branch changes look like pull-request changes, consuming macOS runners and adding irrelevant checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The three Periphery scope jobs now compare GitHub's synthetic pull-request merge commit with its first parent, which is the exact base tree used to build that merge result. Checkout depth is increased to two so both commits are available; the stale event-base fetch is no longer needed.

Scope behavior remains fail-closed, manual dispatch still scans, draft pull requests still skip, and renamed files remain covered.

## User Impact

Unrelated pull requests no longer start iOS, macOS, or shared OpenClawKit Periphery scan jobs solely because `main` changed. Pull requests that actually touch the scoped native paths continue to run the same scans.

AI-assisted change; I reviewed and understand the implementation and tests.

## Evidence

- Regression test builds a hermetic synthetic merge where `main` adds a shared OpenClawKit file while the PR changes only docs. The old event-base comparison reports a scoped change; `HEAD^1..HEAD` reports only the PR's docs file and sets `should-scan=false`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/periphery-scope-workflows.test.ts test/scripts/ios-periphery-comment-workflow.test.ts test/scripts/periphery-intersection.test.ts` — 3 files, 36 tests passed.
